analysis.estimand: A positive partial correlation of per_iteration_cost (wall_seconds/iterations) with excess/p ((columns_generated-k)/p) after controlling for k/p, log(iterations), lambda_ratio and condition, within screened subsets of cg_hist cells per family.
analysis.population: cg_hist solves in families sparse, illcond, toeplitz, block.
analysis.target_claim: Per-round CG cost is driven by active-set size (columns_generated beyond planted k), not just generic problem-size/iteration-count scaling.
analysis.unanalysable_reason: The idea's primary statistic and every covariate it needs are per-record arithmetic transforms of two or more raw fields -- per_iteration_cost = wall_seconds/iterations, k/p, excess/p = (columns_generated-k)/p, and log(iterations) -- and the closed reduction language has no operation that builds such a per-record derived field. 'ratio' and 'difference' combine two EARLIER scalar reductions (already-aggregated numbers), not two fields of the same record; 'ols_coefficient' terms and response are restricted to a literal field name or the product of two field names, so neither a ratio (k/p, excess/p, wall_seconds/iterations) nor a log transform (log(iterations)) can appear as a term or response; and 'correlation' is Pearson on two raw fields, not Spearman and not a partial correlation controlling for several covariates simultaneously beyond a single linear OLS term. Consequently none of per_iteration_cost, k/p, excess/p or log(iterations) -- the quantities the whole falsifier is built on -- can be constructed from the fields cg.cells@1 declares (wall_seconds, iterations, columns_generated, k, p, lambda_ratio, condition) under the operations this schema allows, so the estimand cannot be computed regardless of what command or grid the design chooses. This caps every measurement of this idea at INSUFFICIENT; the capability would need to emit per-record derived ratio/log fields, or the analysis language would need a per-record transform/residualization primitive, before this question is analysable.

hypothesis.core_idea: columns_generated/p is near-collinear with k/p under exact support recovery, so it cannot separate an active-set-size mechanism from generic problem-size scaling (the parent idea's failure mode). excess = columns_generated-k is identically zero under exact recovery and only departs from zero in not-ok or high-lambda_ratio cells, giving a regressor not mechanically tied to k/p by construction. Test whether per_iteration_cost still moves with excess/p once k/p, iteration count, lambda_ratio and condition are removed, restricting the test to family-screened subsets with pre-specified, quantile-based (not data-peeked) thresholds so that failing the screen is reported as inconclusive rather than silently testing degenerate data, and reporting a mandatory diagnostic for whether the screened subsample re-entangles excess/p with log(iterations).
hypothesis.falsifier: Per family: (1) select cg_hist cells not-ok-but-attempted OR lambda_ratio >= family's own 75th percentile (rule fixed in advance, not chosen post hoc). (2) If within-family IQR(|excess|/p) does not exceed 4/median(p) (pre-registered floor = 2x the 1/p quantization step), report that family inconclusive and exclude it from the verdict. (3) In passing families, fit per_iteration_cost ~ k/p + log(iterations) by OLS, compute the Spearman partial correlation of residuals with excess/p; refit adding lambda_ratio and condition and recompute. (4) Mandatory diagnostic: compute Spearman corr(excess/p, log(iterations)) in the same subsample; if |corr| > 0.8, label that family 'confounded-inconclusive' regardless of sign. The hypothesis is falsified if, among families passing both the IQR screen and the confound diagnostic, none shows a significant (p<0.05) positive partial correlation of per_iteration_cost with excess/p after controlling for k/p, log(iterations), lambda_ratio and condition, or the correlation is significant only before adding lambda_ratio/condition. A surviving positive result is consistent with the mechanism but, since cg.cells@1 has no per-round trajectory field, cannot alone discriminate it from the named rival accounts -- the test is asymmetric: it can kill the hypothesis but a positive result remains a multi-way tie among mechanisms.
hypothesis.mechanism: If per-round cost is driven by the size of the active column set that must be priced/refreshed each CG round, cells carrying more or fewer columns than the planted k should show elevated or reduced per_iteration_cost even after k/p, iteration count, lambda_ratio and condition are held fixed, because excess carries active-set-bloat information those covariates do not fully absorb. A pure problem-size-scaling account predicts excess/p is residual noise once k/p and difficulty covariates are fixed.
hypothesis.research_question: Within cg.cells@1 records for solver cg_hist in families {sparse, illcond, toeplitz, block}, restricted per family to cells that are not-ok-but-attempted OR have lambda_ratio at or above that family's own 75th percentile (among cg_hist cells): after regressing per_iteration_cost = wall_seconds/iterations on k/p and log(iterations), does the residual retain a significant positive partial (Spearman) correlation with excess/p = (columns_generated-k)/p, and does this partial correlation survive adding lambda_ratio and condition as covariates, in at least one family whose within-family IQR(|excess|/p) exceeds 4/median(p) (a pre-registered floor set at twice the quantization step 2/p, since excess is integer-valued)?
hypothesis.title: Per-iteration cost in cg_hist and active-set overshoot: does excess/p = (columns_generated-k)/p carry residual signal beyond k/p and iteration count?
